title: Pointers and Arrays
learningObjectives: Explain array-to-pointer conversion and pointer traversal.
Advance pointers by elements rather than bytes.
Use pointer indexing and begin/end ranges safely.
Prefer range-based iteration when manual pointers add risk.

understand.concept: Array names can convert to pointers to their first element in many expressions. Pointer traversal can access array elements, but an array's size is not carried by the pointer.
understand.whyItMatters: This explains low-level APIs and the relationship between arrays and pointers.
understand.explain: Keep the pointer within the array or one-past-end position; never dereference one-past-end.

examples.explanation: In this expression the array converts to a pointer to its first element.

examples.title: Pointer indexed access
examples.explanation: Pointer indexing is equivalent to *(p+index) within bounds.

examples.title: End pointer range
examples.explanation: The end pointer is one-past-last and is not dereferenced.

practise.guidedTask: For Pointers and Arrays, draw the object and pointer/reference relationships for every example. Mark owner, target, constness, lifetime, validity of access, and any operation that could invalidate the pointer or reference.
practise.independentTask: Write a focused C++ exercise for Pointers and Arrays. Demonstrate at least three cases, including a safe usage and a boundary/invalid case explained in comments but not executed. State who owns the resource and when each object/view is valid.
hints: Draw the pointer/reference and its target object.
Mark whether the object is alive and who owns it.
Check nullptr and bounds before access.
Consider invalidation, deletion and scope exit.
Use standard containers or smart pointers when they express ownership more safely.

questions.explanation: Pointer arithmetic steps by pointee type size.
One-past-end is valid only for limited operations.
Pointer indexing uses dereference of offset.
